Post Title: Rutgers is a great school
Post Body: A lot of people, including students, like to clown on Rutgers, but as a senior graduating in May, I have a very high opinion of the school. From an educational perspective, all my professors have been very knowledgeable and passionate about their jobs. As someone who comes to class everyday ready to learn and participate, I've always felt supported by my professors. I'm not saying all the classes are run perfectly or anything, but I just have a lot of respect for the professors for being so knowledgeable on their specialties, and I honestly feel like the education at this school is top tier. 

I think it's amazing that Rutgers offers so many courses, which allows you to study a variety of topics that you have interest in. I also appreciate how diverse the school is; I've met so many people from different backgrounds and I think it makes the learning environment richer. 

Sure things aren't perfect. I wasn't a huge fan of some of the dorms I've lived in or some of the dining halls and such. But I do believe that Rutgers provides many tools and opportunities for students to succeed and make the most of their experience, at least from an educational and career perspective.
Comment by Major_Honey_4461: I graduated from Rutgers (many years ago) and always believed I got a world class education.  After the first year survey classes, all my classes were small, all my professors were engaged and committed to their students, and the negatives (bad bus service or lousy food in the Commons) had no effect on my ability to get an education.  Even today, you'll not find better bang for the buck than a Rutgers education.

Ohio State and Penn State have great football teams, but last time I looked, football was not the primary mission of a university.

BTW did you know that the Rutgers Philosophy Dept. is consistently ranked in the top three in the world?  Yes.  The world.
Comment by Vegetable_Ear_8440: You get paid to get a PhD
Comment by TheGreenBowlerHat: I agree with all of what you've said.  Glad to know that there are more students who share this viewpoint!
Comment by kufi_schmackah: I graduated from RU in 2020. Always wanted to go to RU since the 6th grade (Pandemonium in Piscataway was the first moment I wanted to go there). I couldn’t wait to get out of the military to go to school there since I had the GI Bill to afford school and ended up loving my time there. I even met my wife at Rutgers. 10/10 experience, would recommend.
Comment by FML63850: Yeah but like, Rutgers can't figure out how to charge and use the GI Bill, it's a shitshow, they can't even get the percentages right and when they do they won't charge the VA the right amount lmao. It's smtg I gotta deal with every semester
Comment by kufi_schmackah: Damn I’m sorry to hear that. I’ve never had an issue. I dealt with Dennis Penny the entire time and he made sure I was taken care of throughout.
Comment by FML63850: Oh yeah no he's awesome, he'll always pull through, it's just the system now, it's a cluster fuck to say the least
Comment by Relatable_Raccoon: The certifying officials are mostly useless in my experience. You've got to constantly be on their ass for everything to line up properly with the VA.
Comment by jcg878: As a Rutgers alum who teaches at another university, I can say that the only group that I've heard disparage Rutgers is its students. It is held in high regard in academic circles.
Comment by IAMLOSINGMYEDGE: I graduated in 2020, and I am so glad I went to Rutgers instead of some out of state school. I remember when I first was going I felt bummed because I wanted to get out of NJ so badly, but looking back it was an awesome experience. You have access to so many opportunities as a big school. The research level of almost all of the programs is great. If I hadn't gone to Rugers I would not have even realized that I had a passion for ecology, and would not have ended up in a PhD program for it. Appreciate your time here everyone!
Comment by Appropriate-Tutor587: Thank you! 🙏🏾
Comment by camillebitch: I LOVE to bitch about rutgers, but here I am transferring over to do my MA because nothing compares to RUTGERS
Comment by WellerFullProof2025: As a parent of a Rutgers student, I echo your comments.  It is easily one of the best educational values in NJ.
Comment by betsywendtwhere: I went to Syracuse for one semester, which I think people view to be a good school, and had some of the worst teachers of my life. I transferred to Rutgers and I can't think of a single teacher I had that was bad. Quite the opposite actually. I remember SO many of my professors having such an impact on me because of how amazing they were. And I've had people shit on me for going to Rutgers but I stand by the fact that it's a fantastic school. I would have had a much worse education at Syracuse, that is pretty much guaranteed. I'm actually considering going to get a masters right now and I immediately thought of Rutgers! I would love to go back.
Comment by IndependentKey7: In the Midwest, when I tell people my kid is at Rutgers, they gasp and get that look like "oh hell I knew he was smart but I didn't know yall were THAT level!" 😂
Comment by No-Light7290: Ppl further away from the school place a lot more respects on its name
Comment by Takeontheworld_: I agree, outside of Middlesex County, Rutgers-NB is considered highly. Its cuz most of the population of students, especially undergrads, are from Middlesex County or in the tri state area.
Comment by theBotKilla: Believing is everything.  Who cares about what others are saying? If Rutgers were good to you, then good for you. There are plenty of graduates who are having great success in their life and many moved on to doctorate program in schools like Harvard, Princeton, MIT, and so on.   Although Rutgers are not t20 school, still its a great school.
Comment by Aromatic_Accident106: Mixed bag
Comment by Patient-Pause3711: I actually dont know why ppl clown rutgers. Its a t40 uni and most everyone does great from it. Lmaoo
Comment by UrBoiKrisp: I think it makes more sense to be called decent rather than great. And in terms of education it comes down to the school and major. Some are good, others not so much.
Comment by slyfoxdmd: Depends on the department. The amount of cheating in the premed classes is disturbing.
Comment by Delicious_Song_: What’s your major?
Comment by dodobrains: I mean I graduated with an IT degree and make 6 figures so I am not complaining.
Comment by zam_1213: Is so good to hear that, I’m an international dentist and this cycle I’m planning to apply for an advanced standing program, Rutgers has one of the strongest programs and hearing this of the school just confirmed it. The only unspoken rule for Rutgers even consider your application and call you for interview is that you need a referral/recommendation from a previous alumni or professor.
Sadly I don’t have it, my friend that just got it is referring a family member, and even with a strong profile and a 4.0 gpa I’m scared to apply and loose my hopes on any chances of getting in.

Now, the Master’s programs are very good, especially for business. Bachelor’s are a dime a dozen today, especially through online schools.
Comment by MRC1986: Agree, Rutgers is awesome.
